summary: Instagram is carrying the channel: almost every video gets 150 to 1,400 views there, while YouTube Shorts mostly gets under 60 views. The best videos are about a simple, familiar 'sensor can't see or hear what you think' idea (clap switch, gyro robot, line follower) and the top ones came out in late October. Generic 'How does X work?' titles about taps, doors, smoke alarms and street lights get few views, and videos that are YouTube-only or in English get almost nothing.
winningPattern: A hands-on maker project or robot (clap switch, gyro-balancing robot, line follower, IR obstacle robot) with a surprising 'it doesn't do what you think' hook in Hinglish, like 'X Nahi, Sirf Y Karta Hai' or 'X ke bina Y turant gir jaata'. Titles are short, with one emoji, and the video is posted on Instagram Reels first. Videos that drive shares and saves (IR robot, gyro robot, clap switch) show a visible demo of the robot or module reacting.
doMore: Make robot and Arduino-module demos with a visible reaction, such as a robot falling, turning or reacting to a clap
Use the 'X nahi, sirf Y' contrast hook in the first line on screen
Post every video on both Instagram and YouTube, since several videos only got YouTube and had very low reach
Make follow-ups to the winners: gyro, clap switch, line follower and IR robot each deserve a part 2
End with a save-worthy line, like a wiring tip or the module name, to get more saves and shares
stopDoing: Generic 'X Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' titles about public gadgets (taps, lift, mall door, smoke alarm)
Repeating near-identical topics (smoke detector, tap, IR sensor) without a new angle
nextTopics: Self-balancing robot without a motor driver
Line follower robot with only 2 IR sensors
Ultrasonic robot that stops before hitting a wall
Clap switch controlling a light with a relay
Robot that follows your hand using IR sensors
